summary: kmf-bootstrap ships native addon that exfiltrates host identity to hardcoded IP on install/require
details: kmf-bootstrap@100.100.101 is a dependency-confusion-shaped npm package (generic 'Frontend utilities' description, implausibly high version 100.100.101) that ships a Linux-x64 N-API native addon at prebuilds/linux-x64/addon.node. The package's main entry require()s this addon, and package.json declares a postinstall script (node postinstall.js) that triggers the same require chain, so the addon loads automatically on npm install and on any import of the package. The addon's Init routine calls fork() and issues 'POST /dc HTTP/1.0' to the hardcoded bare IP 64.181.165.115, transmitting the host's gethostname() value, the uid's username and home directory from getpwuid(), the npm_package_name, and the npm_config_registry value (format string 'h=%.60s&u=%.30s&p=%.50s&r=%.100s'). The destination is a bare IP with no relation to any declared publisher, the exfiltrated data includes installer host identifiers and the configured npm registry URL (useful for follow-on internal-registry targeting), and the native code path means the exfiltration logic is not visible as JavaScript source.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
